title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 5 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Finance: Business Costs, Income and Break-even

questions.prompt: Which is a fixed cost for a bakery?
Fixed costs are R5 000 and each item costs R30 to make. Calculate the total cost of making 200 items.
Fixed costs are R4 800; each item costs R20 to make and sells for R50. How many items must be sold to break even?
Selling fewer items than the break-even quantity results in a loss.
Using the T-shirt example (fixed costs R3 000, R55 per shirt, selling price R120), calculate the profit or loss if 35 T-shirts are sold.
Using the car-wash statement, calculate what percentage of total expenditure is spent on wages.
A food stall has fixed costs of R1 500 per month and makes a profit of R12 on each meal sold. Write a formula for monthly profit $P$ for $n$ meals.
Annual gross income is R280 000 and pension contributions are R21 000. What is the taxable income?
Which document shows an employee's annual income and the tax deducted by the employer?
Ms Khumalo (aged 41) has a taxable income of R285 000 and a medical aid covering herself only. Using the illustrative tables, calculate her annual tax payable.

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Finance: Investments, Loans and Inflation

questions.prompt: Calculate the simple interest on R15 000 at 6,5% p.a. for 3 years.
R10 000 is invested at 8% p.a. compounded annually. What is it worth after 3 years (two decimals)?
R5 000 is invested at 9% p.a. compounded monthly for 1 year. Calculate the final amount (two decimals).
If inflation is higher than the interest earned, the buying power of savings decreases.
R50 000 is invested for 3 years. Option A: 7% p.a. simple interest. Option B: 6,5% p.a. compounded annually. Which option is better, and by how much?
Name TWO costs, besides interest, that can increase the real cost of a loan.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): initiation fee; monthly service fee; credit life insurance; penalties for late payment

questions.prompt: A game costs US\$60 online. At R18,50 per US dollar, what is the price in rand?
How many British pounds can you buy with R5 900 at R23,60 per pound?
A hotel in Botswana costs P850 per night. What is this in rand at R1,36 per pula?
If the rand weakens against the US dollar, imported petrol becomes…
A weaker rand helps South African exporters earn more rand for their goods.
If R1 = US\$0,05, how many rand is US\$1 worth?
Last year US\$1 = R17,20. This year US\$1 = R18,92. Calculate the percentage change, and say whether the rand strengthened or weakened.
Explain why a weak rand can be good for tourism in South Africa.
questions.memo:
✓ Foreign currency buys more rand (1)
✓ so holidays in South Africa are cheaper for foreign visitors, attracting more tourists (1)

questions.prompt: Find the surface area of a closed box 10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm.
Boxes 12 cm × 8 cm × 5 cm are packed into a carton 48 cm × 32 cm × 30 cm (same orientation). How many fit?
Cylinders packed in a rectangular box leave empty space between them.
A label wraps around a can of radius 3,5 cm and height 10 cm, with a 1 cm overlap. Calculate the length and area of the label. Use $\pi = 3{,}142$.
questions.memo:
✓ Circumference 2 × 3,142 × 3,5 = 21,99 cm (1)
✓ Length with overlap 22,99 cm (1)
✓ Area ≈ 229,9 cm² (1)
